reasoning: The two sets share the same skeleton: the same 3 stages, the same 3 milestones, 6 pipelines, 31 M1 tasks, nearly identical pipelines and layout. Set B is a cleaned and corrected version, and Set A still carries contradictions and process leftovers. In Set A the brief says every agent 'clearly beats both' baselines while the spec only asks dqn-compact to be not worse than scripted. The fish-tank ideas doc says every rung beats scripted while spec EVAL-07 only asks this of rungs 2 and 3. The contract's RunSettings says ppo works 'only with the tank', yet predator-prey requires ppo. Chart has no label field, yet TC-70 needs a 'reported' label. Snake.reset_to returns a bare ndarray against the team-keyed Env. lab.main has no --smoke flag, yet every smoke command uses it. with_seed is acceptance-tested but missing from the contract. The M1 Exit lists TC-15 both in the TC-01–TC-25 range and among the real-run checks. AD-09 and AD-13 still say 'adopted before M1 is built' / 'Replan of its interface task', and the plan keeps Replan notes. On RL soundness Set B is stronger. It runs non-inferiority tests uncorrected, since correcting them would make 'not worse' easier to pass, and TC-23(c) tests this. It fixes GAE so a truncated game bootstraps from its own last state and advantages don't carry into the next game. It makes the SB3 PPO action Box unbounded so the library and the hand-written PPO send the tank the same actions. On the plan, Set B's packets carry the needed types: Set A's M1-T06 train spine leaves out Transition, StepResult, TeamSpec, SOLO and create_run. Set B sizes DQN and Snake honestly (M and S, not XS), adds a real file edge between T26 and T27, which both edit agents/dqn/agent.py, and gives M2 and M3 checkable Exit lines. Set B's weaknesses: the M1 interface task freezes M2/M3 symbols (FishTank, PPOAgent, PredatorPrey), and the brief softens the scripted bar to 'matches or beats'.

strengths: Clear value → policy-gradient → self-play ladder, with random and scripted baselines and a library comparison at every stage
Strong closed-form golden cases (Q-update, returns-to-go, GAE, clipped objective, reflection, view layouts)
Single shared core with teams and batch-first arrays, so all three environments use one training loop
Readable pipeline step tables with entry sketches
weaknesses: Many contradictions across brief, ideas, spec, contract and tests (scripted-beat bar, ppo/predprey, Chart label, reset_to return type, --smoke)
Stale process text left in (AD-09/AD-13 'adopted before M1 is built', Replan notes, a risk about the teams revision 'rippling into M1')
M2 and M3 have no Exit criteria in the roadmap
Spine packets miss types they need (T06 has no Transition or StepResult); DQN spine and Snake rules sized XS
Multiple-comparison correction applied to 'not worse' claims, which makes them easier to pass

strengths: Brief, spec, architecture, contract and tests agree; stale replan framing removed
Correct statistics: 'beats' claims corrected, 'not worse' claims uncorrected, scope of pooled claims stated, TC-23(c) guards it
GAE segment and truncation handling and the PPO action-bound parity with SB3 are spelled out
Packets include all frozen types the task touches; realistic sizes; real T26→T27 file edge
M2 and M3 have checkable Exit lines
weaknesses: M1-T01 freezes M2/M3 symbols (FishTank, PPOAgent, PredatorPrey, OpponentPool), so the interface task is larger than M1 needs
Brief softens the ground-truth 'beats scripted' to 'matches or beats', relying on EVAL-04's 'at least one Snake agent'
Contract is ~460 lines in one package; heavy reading for a solo learner
A phase 0 interface plus 30 tasks is a lot of ceremony for one Snake milestone
